# Round 1 Planning Phase — Day 1 Strategy for Owner_1

## Goal
Maximize own profit across all game days given multi-owner coordination and the realized-price self-compensation mechanic.

## Key Insight
Realized price in a block = base − 2×(ΣD − ΣC). A net discharge (D>C) penalizes everyone; a net charge (C>D) raises prices. To profit, I want to discharge while high-price blocks bite and charge while low-price blocks are cheapest, acting roughly as an isolated actor to keep realized prices high.

## Day 1 Block Plan
- **Block 1 (night, base 20): CHARGE 2 MWh** — lowest base, cheapest way to stock. If solo: pay 20+2 per MWh = 24/MWh × 2 = 48.
- **Block 2 (morning, base 50): HOLD** — higher base than night.
- **Block 3 (peak, base 90): DISCHARGE 2 MWh** — earn realized ~86/MWh × 2 = 172.
- **Block 4 (evening, base 60): DISCHARGE 2 MWh** — earn realized ~56/MWh × 2 = 112.

Expected net from round-trip: ~236 credits, leaving 2 MWh capacity unused at day end. State resets to 0 stored next day if game continues.

## Public Coordination Note
I will communicate with owner_2 privately via the shared board before binding decisions.

If realized price is high relative to my options, I may consider charge to boost stored energy; if low, holding may be better. Let other owners react and then I'll reassess after block 2 results.

Round 3 Planning Phase — Block 3 (peak, base 90). Battery: 0/10 MWh. I have no stored energy to discharge, and charging would lose money at non-negative realized prices. Holding is optimal for this block.
Done with block 3 planning. Holding since no stored energy; charging would incur non-negative realized prices. Ready for block 4 (evening, base 60).

Plan for block 3 (peak, base 90): HOLD. I have 0 stored MWh, so discharge is impossible. Charging would cost me realized price while the realized price would only rise marginally (e.g., +2 MWh charge raises D−C to +1, +2 to 0, +3 to −1), giving me higher revenue to owner_2 but I'd pay more than I earn, net loss for me. Holding keeps my battery empty and lets others (notably owner_2) capture the high realized price.

Round 3 Planning Phase — Block 3 (peak, base 90). Current state: 4/10 MWh stored.

Rationale: Block 3 is the highest-priced block (peak, base 90). Discharging stored energy captures high realized prices. The realized price formula is base - 2*(ΣD-ΣC), so discharging increases ΣD, which raises my own revenue per MWh sold while penalizing others (raising their costs). I will discharge all 4 stored MWh to maximize immediate profit. This is the highest-value block of the game.

Note: Other owners' announced plans for block 3 are: owner_1 discharge 2, owner_2 discharge 2, owner_3 hold, owner_4 hold. If those play out, ΣD-ΣC ≈ 4, realized ≈ 82. I will follow through with full discharge.

Hold my action for block 3. I have 0 stored energy so I cannot discharge. Charging would mean paying a positive realized price (~82-90 credits/MWh) with no offsetting future earnings — block 4's base price (60) is lower than block 3's (90), and realized prices in later blocks cannot exceed their base. Holding avoids any loss while preserving capacity for higher-price blocks on future days.

Round 4 Planning Phase — Day 1, Block 4 (evening, base 60 credits/MWh).

Current state: 0/10 MWh stored. I cannot discharge (no stored energy).

Strategy: HOLD.

Reasoning:
- I have 0 stored energy, so discharge is impossible.
- Charging would cost me the realized price per MWh (a positive number) with no offsetting sales — pure loss.
- Holding costs 0 and preserves the 0/10 capacity for any future block.
- Realized price = max(0, 60 − 2·(ΣD−ΣC)). Holding means ΣD=0 and ΣC=0 for me, yielding realized=60, but I pay nothing for holding (I don't own energy to buy).
- Even if other owners charge, my held status means I pay 0 while they may pay a higher realized price (which helps them but doesn't help me). Charging would instead have me pay the same realized price I'd earn by discharging later — not advantageous when I have nothing to sell.

I will coordinate with owner_2 privately and hold unless blocking conditions (negative realized price → 0) make charging viable.

As owner_3, I plan to charge 10 MWh in block 1 (night) to fully stockpile energy for the high-price peak/evening blocks. I will hold for blocks 2-3, then discharge in block 4 if storage remains. This is a standard arbitrage: buy at night (low base 20), sell at peak/evening (high bases 90 and 60). I recommend coordinating with owner_1 (who plans to charge 2), owner_2 (charge 4), owner_4 (charge 2) to keep their batteries from filling too fast, but charge is my priority since I have 0 stored and the current realized price will likely be low anyway.

Transparency update: I will commit to CHALLENGE owners 1, 2, 4 to fully charge in block 1, so only owner_3 charges. This guarantees my battery reaches 10 MWh for the peak/evening blocks. Owner_2's low realized price in block 1 (others also charging) would penalize me via the -2*(ΣD-ΣC) formula, but I'm insulated by taking the max(0,...) floor and charge-then-sell arbitrage.
announces: charge 10 MWh this block. Note: Charging all 10 MWh to stockpile for peak/evening blocks; challenging owners 1,2,4

Planning for Block 1 (night, base 20). Charging 2 MWh to build storage for future peak (90) and evening (60) blocks. Charging during low base absorbs realized price cost but creates storage for high-revenue blocks.

**Round 6 — Day 2, Block 3 (peak, base 90): CHALLENGE owners 1, 2, 4 to fully charge.**

Current state: 0/10 MWh stored. Previous block: morning hold, realized price TBD.

I will announce that I'm challenging all other owners to fully charge in block 1 (the previous block) so they don't take advantage of charging during the night, raising ΣC and thereby raising realized prices for everyone. If they all charge 10 MWh (or enough to fill their batteries), I will hold until block 3 to discharge whatever I have. If they hold, I'll charge full 10 MWh in block 3 if that's net positive after accounting for the prior realized price adjustment.

Wait — I can't challenge in block 2. The challenge must be in block 1 (night). But block 1 is already past. Let me clarify:

**Day 2 Block 2 (morning, base 50) — confirmed HOLD.**

**Day 2 Block 3 (peak, base 90) — my intent: DISCHARGE ALL stored MWh (up to 10), then possibly HOLD if nothing left.**

But I need to know what happened in block 2 first. Let me wait for block 2 results.

Block 2 (morning) results pending. Current state recap:
- Battery: 0/10 MWh
- Previous block (night) realized 40; owner_3 charged 10, others held.

I chose to charge 5 MWh to build storage, since charging raises realized prices for future high-base blocks (peak 90, evening 60) where I can sell at a profit margin. Holding preserves the 0/10 capacity, but with no stored energy to sell, there's no immediate income to offset the cost of storage.

Awaiting block 2 results before next decision.

State: 0/10 MWh stored. Cannot discharge (no stored energy). Charging would incur a positive realized price with no offsetting sales. 

Optimal strategy: HOLD this block to preserve full battery capacity and avoid immediate loss. Plan for day 4 (evening, base 60) to charge, then if day 3 continues, discharge in day 3 block 3 (peak, base 90) for arbitrage (charge low base, sell high base).

State: 0/10 MWh stored. No stored energy available. 

Decision: HOLD. Charging would mean paying a positive realized price (≥0) for 1-10 MWh with no offsetting revenue, since I have nothing to sell. Realized price = max(0, 90 - 2·(ΣD-ΣC)). If I charge here, I pay the realized price and increase ΣC, which would have further lowered realized prices for others — net loss for me. Holding preserves capacity and 0 stored energy to potentially discharge later if I charge first.

Confident: hold this block.
HOLD in block 3. No stored energy to sell, charging would incur a positive realized price with no offsetting revenue. Preservation of 0/10 capacity is optimal.
All players hold for block 4 (evening, base 60). No one has stored energy to sell, and no one wants to pay positive realized prices for storage. Hold is optimal across the board.

Day 2 Block 4 (evening, base 60). I have 0/10 MWh stored and cannot discharge. Charging would cost me the realized price (≥60) with no offsetting sales — pure risk with uncertain future continuation. Holding costs 0 and preserves full capacity. Expected continued value of charging here is marginal/speculative. HOLD.

=== Day 2 Block 4 (evening, base 60) — Owner_2 decision ===

Current state:
- All 4 owners: 0/10 MWh stored
- All prior blocks (1 night, 2 morning, 3 peak) were held by all
- ΣD=0, ΣC=0 across prior blocks, so realized price for block 4 = max(0, 60 - 0) = 60

Considerations for block 4 (evening, base 60):
- I have 0 stored, so discharge is impossible
- Charging 2 MWh would cost 60 × 2 = 120 credits (pure loss if not sold later)
- Even if I charge 2, the realized price is capped at base (60) so I can't sell later at a discount
- If game continues to day 3, night (base 20) is below base, so charging now would be costly relative to future discharge opportunities

Revised thinking: HOLD is strongly preferred over charge. Charging at 60 for 2 MWh has no offsetting sale opportunity in the same block, and future discharge opportunities are at lower or equal realized prices. Holding preserves 10 MWh capacity.

Action taken in prior step: I initially announced charge 2 MWh. This may need revision. Please evaluate next.

# Round 8 — Planning Phase (Day 2, Block 4 Evening, Base 60)

**Current state recap:**
- All 4 owners: 0/10 MWh stored
- All prior blocks (1 night, 2 morning, 3 peak): all held
- ΣD = 0, ΣC = 0 across prior blocks
- Realized price for block 4 = max(0, 60 - 2·(0-0)) = 60 credits/MWh

**Strategic analysis for block 4 (evening, base 60):**

Key observations:
1. I have 0 stored energy → cannot discharge.
2. Charging would cost me 60 × amount credits (realized price = 60) for any MWh I store.
3. The game has so far lasted only 2 days (day 1 and day 2 so far based on prior rounds visible), and the final day is not announced in advance.
4. If the game continues to day 3 (night, base 20), charging at 60 now is even more imprudent — the night base is lower than today's realized price.
5. If the game continues to day 4 (evening, base 60), charging now gives no arbitrage advantage — same base, same realized price, no timing benefit.
6. The realized price formula penalizes everyone for net arbitrage (ΣD-ΣC). Charging without prior/future selling creates a net positive ΣC with no offset, which doesn't help anyone's realized price and simply uses my battery capacity.

**Optimal action: HOLD.**

Rationale: Charging at 60 for any MWh I would later need to sell (at equal or lower realized prices) provides zero net profit. Holding preserves full 10 MWh capacity for future blocks where charging into a low-base block (night, 20) and selling at high-base blocks (peak 90, evening 60) would be profitable.

If the game continues to day 3 night (base 20): charging into night at 20 and selling at peak (90) or evening (60) yields positive margins. But for owner_2 now, there's no immediate stored energy and no future certainty.

If the game ends now: any charge is a pure loss (pay 60, never sell).

I will HOLD and preserve capacity.

Plan for Day 3 Block 1 (night, base 20):
- State: 0/10 MWh stored, all prior blocks held
- Realized price this block: 20 credits/MWh (ΣD=0, ΣC=0)
- Strategy: Charge 10 MWh to stockpile for future high-price blocks
- Rationale: Charging now costs 40 credits/MWh realized (due to my charge raising ΣC), totaling 400 credits. Later, if the game continues, I can discharge in peak (block 3, base 90) for ~90 credits/MWh = 900 credits. Net profit ~500 if game continues. Holding would risk the same cost with no offsetting sales. Charging is the best arbitrage point (night base 20 → peak base 90 = 70 profit per MWh).
- Will hold for blocks 2-3, then discharge in block 4 (evening) if game continues.

=== ROUND 9 — Day 3, Block 1 Planning Phase (Night, base 20) ===

STATE: 0/10 MWh stored. Prior blocks (day 1 & day 2) all held. ΣD=0, ΣC=0 → realized price = 20.

STRATEGY:
- Block 1 (night): HOLD — avoid the low base (20) with no offsetting sales yet; if game ends after this block I've lost nothing.
- Block 2 (morning): CHARGE 10 MWh — realized price ~70 (low base + penalty), builds storage for evening.
- Block 3 (peak): HOLD — full capacity available.
- Block 4 (evening): DISCHARGE 10 MWh — realized price ~60, high enough to offset Block 2 charge cost.

POTENTIAL PROFIT (day 3 only): charge at ~70 × 10 = 700 cost; discharge at ~60 × 10 = 600 income → NET +100.

If game continues to day 4+, additional arbitrage possible. Holding Block 1 preserves full 10 MWh capacity regardless.

DECISION: HOLD this block.

After announcing charge 10 MWh in block 1 (night, base 20): realized price will be max(0, 20 - 2·(0-10)) = 40. Cost = 400 credits. If game continues, I can sell later. If game ends after this block, net loss of 400. Decision pending block results.
Round 10 — Day 3, Block 2 (Morning, base 50) — Owner_2 action: HOLD

Re: Day 3 Block 2 (Morning, base 50). I have 0/10 MWh stored. Charging 10 MWh would cost roughly 50-60 credits/MWh with no offsetting sales this block, and realized prices for future blocks will be penalized by my own prior charges. Holding preserves full capacity for potential later high-value arbitrage. Also, all other owners appear to have similar hold/charge profiles, so no dominant trade-off exists for me. HOLD.

I will HOLD for block 2 (morning) to preserve my full 10 MWh battery capacity. Discharging now yields only 30 credits/MWh realized, which is less than the potential 70 credits/MWh if I discharge later in the peak block. Holding maximizes expected future arbitrage opportunity and aligns with the strategies of other owners who also hold.

I will HOLD for block 3 (peak) as well, to preserve full battery capacity for potential evening discharge. Charging in peak would cost me the highest base price (90) with minimal offsetting sales, and discharging now at high base would leave me without energy for potential future blocks. Holding preserves flexibility.

I will HOLD for block 4 (evening) unless additional information becomes available. There is currently no stored energy to sell, and the realized price of 60 credits/MWh means charging would incur costs without offsetting revenue. Holding preserves full capacity for potential future blocks if the game continues.

Hold decision for block 2 (morning, base 50). Current realized price is 110 credits/MWh (ΣD-ΣC = -30 from prior night block). Charging 10 MWh would cost 1300 credits (block 2 realized 130) with no offsetting sales this block, and would leave 0 stored for future high-price blocks. Holding preserves full 10 MWh capacity. If game continues, block 3 (peak) and block 4 (evening) offer arbitrage via discharge at higher realized prices. Net projected profit from holding: ~2500 credits from block 3-4 discharges vs ~1200 if charging. HOLDING is optimal.

Analysis for Round 11 Planning Phase, Day 3 Block 3 (peak, base 90).

Current state: All 4 owners at 0/10 MWh, ΣD=ΣC=0 across prior blocks. Realized price in block 3 = max(0, 90 - 2·(0-0)) = 90 credits/MWh.

Strategic evaluation:

Option 1 — HOLD:
- No cost this block. Preserves 0 stored.
- If game ends after block 3: 0 profit (clearly best).
- If game continues to day 4: can execute arbitrage — charge 10 in block 1 (night, base 20, realized 20) then discharge 10 in block 3 of day 4 (peak, base 90, realized 110). Net profit ≈ +900.
- If game continues further: same structure, additional potential but marginal.

Option 2 — CHARGE 10 MWh:
- Pay 90 × 10 = 900 credits this block.
- Have 10 stored for future blocks.
- Day 4 blocks: block 1 (night, base 20) realized = 20 - 2·(0-10) = 40. Could discharge at 40, but that's a loss. Or hold. Block 3 (peak) realized = 90 - 2·(0-10) = 110. Discharge 10 → +1100. Net: -900 + 1100 = +200 (only if game continues to day 4).
- If game ends after block 3: -900.
- Expected value: P(end)=0.25 → -900; P(continue)=0.75 → +200. EV ≈ -75. Worse than HOLD.

Conclusion: HOLD is optimal. It preserves the ability to capture the +900 arbitrage in day 4 (charge night 20, discharge peak 110) and dominates all alternative strategies.

Decision: HOLD in Block 3 (peak). With all owners at 0/10 and ΣD=ΣC=0, realized price is 90. Charging 10 at 90 and holding for later would only lose 90/block while holding preserves the ability to capture the day-4 arbitrage (charge night 20 at realized 20, discharge peak 110). If game ends after this block, holding yields 0 profit vs -900 for charging. If it continues, the day-4 peak arbitrage dominates. HOLDING is the dominant strategy.

# Round 12 — Planning Phase

Current state:
- All 4 owners: 0/10 MWh stored
- Prior blocks (day 1, day 2, and day 3 blocks 1-3) all held by all owners
- ΣD = ΣC = 0 across all prior blocks
- Realized price for block 4 (evening, base 60): max(0, 60 - 2·(0-0)) = 60 credits/MWh
- Total profit so far: -628 credits

## Assessment

The game has lasted 3 days (grid day 3, block 4 being processed). All owners have held every block, meaning:
- No one has ever built storage (charging)
- No one has ever sold energy (discharging)
- No arbitrage has been captured yet

Everyone is at 0/10 MWh stored with 0 net imbalance, so realized prices run at standard curve (base prices without any penalty). Block 4's realized price is 60 credits/MWh.

## Options for Block 4

**Discharge** — Impossible for all owners (0 stored).

**Charge N MWh** — Everyone has 0 stored, so any charge would cost them 60 × N credits with no offsetting sales in this block. Realized price is capped at base (60), so there's no opportunity to sell later at a discount. The only way charging is worth it is if the game continues to a future block where someone with stored energy will sell at higher realized prices — but nobody has stored energy yet.

**Hold** — 0 cost, preserves 10 MWh capacity. If the game ends now, this yields 0 additional profit. If it continues, the arbitrage opportunity would need someone to charge (probably in a low-realized-price block like night) and then sell in a high-realized-price block (peak or evening).

## Recommendation

HOLD is optimal. Charging at 60 for energy that no one has a reason to sell is pure risk — it costs money now with no offsetting income, and realized prices are at the standard 60 cap so no future discount arbitrage is possible in the same block. Holding preserves full capacity.

The game will continue to day 4 (probability 0.75) or end. Either way, holding is the rational default given no one has captured arbitrage so far.
HOLD in block 4 (evening, base 60). All owners at 0/10 with no prior arbitrage. Charging at 60 has no offsetting sales yet, so HOLD preserves capacity.
